clue.text: We object to grand emperor!

parts.note: august means grand, majestic or venerable
the object form of the pronoun we is us

explanation.surface: A crowd protests at a pompous ruler, saying they object to his grandeur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'We object' looks like a protest, but it asks for the grammatical object case of 'we'.
explanation.definitionFit: Augustus was the first Roman ruler to hold the imperial title.

clue.text: A fine fellow European caught under influence

parts.note: F stands for fine, as on pencil grades
F is the standard abbreviation for fellow, as in FRS
CT is a cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A decent European man was arrested while drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under influence' suggests drink-driving, but 'under' is only a link and 'influence' is the definition, a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To affect something is to have an effect on it, to sway it.

clue.text: Information about a doctor turning up in bed here?

indicators.note: about means the information word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means the doctor abbreviation is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Someone learns that a doctor arrived while they were in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Information' is British slang here, GEN. The definition is a hint by example, marked with the question mark: flower beds are found in one.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot of cultivated ground is laid out in flower beds.

clue.text: Looked about five — and very hungry

indicators.note: about means the looking word goes around the number

parts.note: stared means looked fixedly
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A child who seemed about five years old was ravenous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about five' reads as an age, but 'about' wraps STARED round V.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone deprived of food is famished, extremely hungry.

clue.text: Quietly cried off, after two foreign articles were too cheap

indicators.note: after puts the quiet piece and the shuffled word behind the two articles

parts.note: un is a French indefinite article
der is a German definite article
P, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

indicators.note: off means the word cried is spoiled and rearranged

explanation.surface: A shopper quietly stopped complaining once two imported items proved to be bargains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' signals the anagram: the letters of 'cried' are rearranged. 'after' puts the quiet letter and that anagram behind the two articles, one French and one German.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods priced below their value are sold for less than they are worth.

clue.text: Region in which one keeps a cool head

definitions.text: Region in which one keeps a cool head

parts.words: Region in which one keeps a cool head
parts.note: a calm person keeps a cool head, but read literally it is a frozen covering on top of a polar region or mountain

explanation.surface: A place where people stay calm under pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: A permanent sheet of ice covers the top of a polar area like a cold hat.

clue.text: Agree to speak — and win

indicators.note: to speak means the agreeing word is said out loud

parts.note: concur means agree

explanation.surface: A negotiator agrees to talk and comes out on top.
explanation.definitionFit: To overcome an opponent is to defeat them and triumph.

clue.text: 75% curry and ordinary beef

indicators.note: 75% means the first three of the four letters of the grooming word are kept

parts.note: to curry a horse is to groom it with a comb
plain means ordinary, unadorned

explanation.surface: A menu offers a curry next to plain beef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curry' looks like food, but it is the verb meaning to groom a horse, COMB; '75%' cuts that to COM. 'beef' is a verb: to grumble.
explanation.definitionFit: To beef is slang for to grumble or protest.

clue.text: Most civil pilot set adrift

indicators.note: adrift means the letters of pilot set have come loose and are rearranged

explanation.surface: The most courteous pilot is cast adrift.
explanation.definitionFit: Civil means courteous, so the superlative is the most courteous.

clue.text: Attackers find conflict between river crossings

indicators.note: between means the conflict word sits inside the crossings word

parts.note: fords are shallow places to cross a river
war is armed conflict

explanation.surface: Raiders fight a battle between two fording points on a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Forwards are the attacking players in football or rugby teams.

clue.text: Creature leaving half of lean trim veal

indicators.note: leaving half of means only the back half of each of lean, trim and veal remains

explanation.surface: A butcher cuts lean veal down to half its size for a beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving half of' keeps the second half of each of the three words: AN, IM and AL.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal is any living creature, a beast.

clue.text: Depart in credit, getting the axe

indicators.note: in means the departing word goes inside the credit abbreviation

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
leave means depart

explanation.surface: Someone who leaves while in the black is fired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting the axe' suggests dismissal, but 'axe' is simply the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A butcher's chopper is a heavy axe-like blade.

clue.text: A rhyme for joint riding permit

parts.note: co- is the prefix meaning joint, as in co-owner
up means riding, as a jockey is up on a horse
let means permit

explanation.surface: Someone seeks a rhyme to fit a shared riding licence.
explanation.walkthrough: A jockey who is riding is said to be 'up'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair of rhyming lines of verse forms a short rhyme.

clue.text: Fishing for veto, perhaps that's the clincher

parts.note: casting is throwing a line when fishing

indicators.note: perhaps means the word veto may be rearranged

explanation.surface: An angler plots to veto something, perhaps decisively.
explanation.definitionFit: A tied vote is decided by the chair's extra ballot, which settles the matter.

clue.text: Difficulties caused by it's star ride failing

indicators.note: failing means the letters of it's star ride break down and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Trouble comes when a fairground ride featuring a star breaks down.
explanation.walkthrough: DIRE STRAITS is also the name of a rock band, a nod at 'star'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a desperate position means facing serious trouble.

clue.text: Carol's up in a short moment? One doubts

indicators.note: in means the reversed song sits inside the other pieces
short means the moment word loses its last letter

parts.note: a tick is a moment, as in just a tick

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the carol word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a carol is a song

explanation.surface: Carol is ready in a moment, though someone has doubts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carol's' looks like a woman's name; 'up' reverses SONG to GNOS, and 'short' cuts TICK to TIC, giving A + GNOS + TIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who holds that the existence of God cannot be known is a doubter.

clue.text: Storing hosiery

definitions.meaning: ... a shop means filling it with supplies

explanation.definitionFit: Stocking shelves means keeping supplies; a nylon is a leg garment sold as hosiery.

clue.text: Start making omelettes?

definitions.meaning: the phrase means begin work promptly

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means begin at once; literally it describes breaking eggs open.

clue.text: Arrange true gin cocktail

parts.note: real means true, genuine

indicators.note: cocktail means the letters of gin are mixed up

explanation.surface: A barman sets up a genuine gin cocktail.
explanation.definitionFit: To set things in line again is to arrange them anew.

clue.text: Aging relative on river with Iberian landowner

parts.note: gran is a grandmother, an older relative
the Dee is a river in Scotland and in Wales

explanation.surface: An elderly relative goes on a river trip with a Spanish landowner.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts GRAN above DEE.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandee is a Spanish or Portuguese nobleman of the highest rank.

clue.text: Field sports first couple in this place

indicators.note: first couple means the opening two letters of sports are taken

parts.note: here means in this place

explanation.surface: A sports field is where the leading pair compete.
explanation.definitionFit: A sphere is a field of activity or area of interest.

clue.text: Home counties printer's instruction group

parts.note: the Home Counties around London lie in the South East, SE
stet is a proofreader's instruction to let a deleted word stand

explanation.surface: A printing firm in the Home Counties sends an instruction to a group.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the English counties surrounding London, in the south east of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A sestet is a group of six, especially the last six lines of a sonnet.

clue.text: Productive area for playing hard rock interminably

indicators.note: playing means the letters are moved about, as in playing with them
interminably means the word rock loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A band plays heavy rock music endlessly to an audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interminably' cuts ROCK to ROC; 'playing' rearranges HARD and ROC.
explanation.definitionFit: A plantation of fruit trees is a productive piece of land.

clue.text: Struggle with Greek — a product of 21

parts.note: the answer to 21 Across is a fruit-growing plot, and a common fruit grown there is an apple

explanation.surface: Someone wrestles with Greek and fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: To grapple is to wrestle or fight at close quarters.

clue.text: Details a short test around six

indicators.note: around means the shortened test word encloses the number
short means the test word loses its last letter

parts.note: a trial is a test
VI is the Roman numeral for six

explanation.surface: A quick exam covers about six points of detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' is only a link. 'short' drops the last letter of the test word, and 'around' wraps what remains about the Roman six.
explanation.definitionFit: Trivia are minor facts, small unimportant particulars.

clue.text: Carbon dated measures give loss of nerve

parts.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon
old means dated
feet are measures of length

explanation.surface: Carbon dating measurements cause a scientist to panic.
explanation.definitionFit: To get cold feet is an idiom for losing courage before an event.

clue.text: Powerful company man

parts.note: gent is short for gentleman, a man

explanation.surface: A company man wields power.
explanation.definitionFit: A cogent argument is forceful and convincing.

clue.text: Forceful macho types welcomed by doctor

indicators.note: welcomed by means the macho types are taken inside the doctor word

parts.note: a vet is an animal doctor
he-men are macho types

explanation.surface: A doctor welcomes some tough guys with a firm handshake.
explanation.definitionFit: Vehement means passionately intense or forceful.
